name: Competitive Basin Ecology Law
purpose: Define interaction dynamics among stabilization basins under finite continuation resources.

candidate_law_statement.informal: Stabilization basins interact when their accessibility domains, reinforcement pathways, or admissibility budgets overlap. Their persistence depends on finite support, compatibility, perturbation resilience, and reconstruction accessibility.

formal.basin_family: 𝔅_U := { B_i : B_i is an active stabilized reconciliation basin in region U }
formal.basin_overlap_condition: Overlap(B_i,B_j) holds when B_i and B_j share accessibility domains, reinforcement channels, transport flux, or admissibility budget.
formal.competition_condition: Compete(B_i,B_j) occurs when simultaneous persistence exceeds shared budget or destabilizes boundary compatibility.
formal.starvation_condition: Starve(B_i) occurs when reinforcement inflow, admissibility margin, or transport accessibility falls below persistence threshold.
formal.cannibalization_condition: Cannibalize(B_i,B_j) occurs when reinforcement of B_i redirects or consumes continuation support previously stabilizing B_j.
formal.co_stabilization_condition: CoStabilize(B_i,B_j) occurs when basins share compatible accessibility topology and reduce mutual drift or boundary pressure.
formal.collapse_propagation_condition: Collapse(B_i) propagates when failure of B_i depletes shared budget, disrupts channels, or increases perturbation load on neighbors.
formal.non_biological_clause: Basin ecology is a structural analogy for interacting continuation basins, not a biological ecology claim.
